newsitem.title: USA: Sony's Dion scores first number one album.
newsitem.headline: Sony's Dion scores first number one album.

text.p: French-Canadian singer Celine Dion scored the first U.S. number one album of her career as "Falling Into You" rose to the top spot in its 28th week on the charts, her label said Wednesday.

The album, released by Sony Corp's Epic Records, sold just over 132,000 copies in the week ended September 22, up from almost 129,000 the week before when it was fourth. All told, more than four million copies have been shipped in the U.S., and worldwide sales stand at more than 11 million copies.

"The number one success of 'Falling Into You' is a triumph both for a truly gifted performer and the dedicated people at her label," said Polly Anthony, president of Epic's 550 Music Music imprint, which handled the Dion album.

550 also claimed the highest new entry in the latest charts as California hard rock band Social Distortion's "White Light, White Heat, White Trash" opened at 27 with sales of almost 30,000. It overshadowed ZZ Top's "Rhythmmen", which opened at 29. ZZ Top record for RCA Records, a unit of Bertelsmann AG .

Last week's number one, New Edition's reunion album, "Home Again", slipped to second, while R.E.M.'s "New Adventures In Hi-Fi" also slipped a notch to third. New Edition record for Seagram Co Ltd's MCA Records and R.E.M. record for Time Warner Inc's Warner Bros. Records.

The late Tupac Shakur continued to storm up the charts. His latest release, "All Eyez On Me", which topped the charts earlier this year, stood at sixth this week from 18th the previous week and 69 the week before. The rapper was killed in a drive-by shooting earlier this month.
